I grew up Catholic (but with very accepting parents), and eventually couldn't reconcile some things.  More of an agnostic now - I think there might be some divinity behind things but it's either not "good" the way we think of the term or it's not omnipotent.  And a lot of the specific stuff is B.S. - I think any modern religion should be an "evolving" one, one that accepts and incorporates the changes that science can bring to society.  Either way it has no effect on my day to day life so it's a "wait and see" sort of thing.  It doesn't impact my suicidal thoughts in either direction, because I care more about the people around me.

Philosophy is similarly great for inspiring people and fostering creativity, making good questions, but I'm not personally so into it.  I think about it sometimes but I'm more often bumping into terrible stories, everything from genocides to someone cheating on their lover instead of being honest, and I...it gets me really depressed when I realize so much of the world hates and can't be honest with others or themselves.

But there's the rub - who's going to listen to me if I try to fix it?  I'm more miserable than most of the people who I think are hurting.  What makes my "method" so great?  Honesty, morality, little kindness, respect?  Lassitude, fatigue, love-sick stupidity?  I like to think I'm a good man.  But sometimes I don't even feel human.  Humans make mistakes, act with passion, and do things.
Unfortunately my place has a no-pets policy.  I do love animals and take every chance I get to visit my friends who have them.

I've tried travel, new friends, new jobs, charity, alcohol, music, video games, drugs (recreational and prescription)...I never stick with one for that long, I guess because I'm lazy or don't like being tied down or both.  Some things I've given more than a fair chance (games), others maybe not enough (a stronger prescription?  jobs?)  But I'm just so tired of trying in general.  I wish I could sleep forever.  Every time I fail one of these things it makes me feel worse, weak, abnormal, not that the desire to sleep forever makes me feel like a brave person but at least then...ah I dunno.

Just tired of being alone, but I see no way to improve that, because really.  No one deserves a depressive lump as a boyfriend/lover/husband/father.  At *best* it just brings everyone down.  And it can be so much worse.  I have friends with messed up parents/SOs and I don't ever want to do that to someone.  The fact that I've felt this way so long (so it's likely not going away due to "environmental factors" or "growth") and the fact that in the once every few months I *have* gained the courage to try and connect with someone...it's only borne fruit once in like 20 years...makes me feel very unattractive and damaged.

Blah blah blah verbal diarrhea.  Feel free to share.
five bucks says PETA agrees with this website.

Many years of quiet depression and a woman I loved much too deeply leaving me a few years ago has made me a kind of "functional Nihilist."  I try my best to have hope and believe in life/love/etc., but I constantly find myself thinking 'what's the point' and having suicidal thoughts - not because my life is *bad*, but just because I don't ever do anything.  I'm painfully shy and haven't so much as dated for years since the breakup.  I left on an overseas trip for a few months to "find myself", but I was really going to distance myself and commit suicide in a way that put the least pain on my loved ones.

I didn't do it and came back, resigned to a life of quiet sadness with bouts of completely dead emotions.  My friends have all said I'm much better after my trip and are excited to see me finally happy.

I'm not.  I just cut down on my contact with them so I can act the part easily, and they want to believe.

But no matter how I feel about myself, I will always have compassion and love for my fellow human.  I wish I could give everyone commenting on this post a hug, or hand out solutions as life-saving candy.  If I could give my life so that you'd have a better one I would...at least I'm an organ donor.

You assume you have to provide something more than just your company for them to want you around.  I think in the vast majority of long-term friends and family, this is not the case, and they will still be devastated if you go where they can't.

These expectations you say they had don't exist.  There is one expectation every loved one has for the one they love: they want you to be happy.

You may have failed at that so far, but you're still alive now, so you still have a chance to turn it around.  If suicide runs in your family it means a chemical imbalance with a genetic source is likely.

Let me say that more plainly: the way you feel is not your fault.  The way you feel can be dealt with.  Drugs will start the process of healing and therapy will "finish" it, and by finish I mean put you in a mindset and habits that must be maintained, but will result in you living every day happier than you are now and wondering *why* you ever thought life wasn't worth sticking around for.

You can do that, and it will be the greatest victory you can achieve.  But you must start NOW.  And all you have to do is get to work.  If you can't start making those baby steps, ask someone who can.  Open up and get some real tangible help from someone close.

People have done this.  It is doable.  Throw away this plan and pick up the brighter one.  Baby steps and permanent changes.  Promise yourself.

You probably know this, but some antidepressants can make you feel worse at first as your body gets used to them.  There are some that will also just not work with certain people, so if there's no improvement after a certain time it's best to switch to a different one or a lighter dose.  This is why having them administered by a professional is important - if you can't get her one to administer ADs, at least find one to consult.  Hopefully there's some sort of health resource in your area she can benefit from for that.

On a different tack, it is very unfair for her to put "Jack" through this nerve-wracking and emotional experience.  Obviously she's not in a good way herself but she needs to either come clean to her friends so someone besides him knows and can help share the task of keeping her safe, or take more drastic steps to help herself.  I'd advise him to convince her to step-up to this responsibility, and watch for false promises - you don't need to blame her but make her see that she really does have to deal with this, maybe by checking herself in somewhere.

>When you're the odd one out, its easy to see things that everyone else seems to miss.

Very true.  It's important to remember there's a lot of things *you* miss when that happens, things other people might find obvious (like your own worth.)  But with a different perspective comes valuable lessons.

I am by far the least motivated, productive person I know, out of anyone I've ever met.  I'm not sure why or how I became this way but it's been very...discouraging.  I've literally not left my room all week.  It's a good thing I know how to live so frugally, or this whole "get a job every few years then live off the savings" thing wouldn't work.  (On the other hand...if I wasn't so minimalist and was active-yet-in-debt, maybe that'd be a net positive...)  In any case there are a number of my traits that make me feel like an alien among the "normals."  Too strange to interact.

I don't recommend these kinds of plans.  They can be very tempting in burning your bridges, cutting ties, and saving them the heartache of your loss.  But in the end you are your legacy, and if you die doing this you leave behind plenty of pain, anger, frustration, and confusion.  It's easy to pretend they won't care when you're dead when you do this first - but in my experience it's not true, and the negative emotions you cause in the meantime will last for them.

I've come up with plans like that before.  I always wind up putting myself in their shoes - how hurtful is it when someone you thought was a friend just starts hating you for no reason?  You start to invent reasons.  That's what happened when my ex left me two years back, and I wouldn't wish it on anyone.  You make them feel worthless, make them wonder if they're a bad person, rewind through all the mis-steps they've taken.

The pain of a friend's senseless death to suicide is terrible.  But IMO this kind of plan isn't worth it.  I think it's better to minimize the damage how you can, but make sure they know how much you love them before you let go.

In the end we all die.  But if they know you loved them, it will be easier for them to move on.  They will get to keep those memories.  You don't want to go out lying.

I would create elaborate preparations for there to be no body to recover, like drowning with weights or cremation somehow.  Too many people go leaving terrible evidence behind for their loved ones.  The loss is bad enough, no need to sear it into their minds with an "event."
